name: Retaining Wall vs Decorative Block Wall: What’s the Difference?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a retaining wall and a decorative block wall on a hillside property?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a retaining wall and a decorative block wall on a hillside property?

acceptedAnswer.text: The key difference is function. A decorative wall is intended mainly for appearance, privacy, or property definition. A retaining wall is engineered to resist soil pressure and keep ground from sliding or eroding. On hillside properties in Los Angeles County, many walls that look like standard block walls actually function as retaining walls because they hold back soil or support a grade change. That means they may need stronger footing, reinforcement, drainage, and permits. If you are planning a wall, ask the contractor whether the design is structural or decorative. A correct classification affects cost, materials, inspections, and long-term safety. It also determines whether drainage and engineering details must be included from the start.
acceptedAnswer.description: A retaining wall is built to hold back soil and resist lateral pressure, while a decorative block wall is mainly for appearance or boundary definition. On a hillside property, a wall that supports earth or a slope is structural, even if it looks decorative. Misclassifying it can lead to failed inspections, drainage problems, or wall movement.
